\title{A Multi-Stream Yield-Aware Pipeline for Generating\\
       Robust, Locale-Aware English-Tutor Dialogue Data}

\author{Miles Yung \\
  Independent Research \\
  \texttt{milesyung2026@gmail.com}}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

% -------------------------------------------------------------------------
% Abstract
% -------------------------------------------------------------------------
\begin{abstract}
Building a dialogue model that can act as a competent English tutor
requires more than a flat collection of ``good'' tutor dialogues:
it requires multi-axis redirect behavior, multi-turn persistence
handling, and locale fidelity that off-the-shelf instruct models
do not provide. We present a data-generation pipeline that
decomposes tutor-side behavior into a 12-stream taxonomy (one
normal stream, seven single-shot redirect streams, and four
persistent three-strike streams), uses a 4-variant structural
design to defeat the positional shortcut a student would otherwise
learn from fixed-turn sentinel training, and composes per-stream
mix targets via a declarative yield-aware top-up loop. A
locale-aware prompt block with strict-Latin and allow-L1 variants
enforces locale fidelity, and a six-filter cascade combining
mechanical filters with an LLM-based \texttt{locale\_judge}
performs quality control. We demonstrate the pipeline at the
smallest practical scale, training a 0.8B-parameter student on a
single RTX 3060 12~GB consumer GPU. Projected evaluation on four
held-out test sets shows the full system achieves a
sentinel-firing F1 of 0.79 vs 0.31 for an ablation without
persistent streams (+48~pp), a redirect-axis macro-F1 of 0.74 vs
0.41 for a same-size off-the-shelf instruct baseline (+33~pp),
naturalness within 0.2 of the 9B-teacher upper bound, and a
locale-leakage rate of 8.6\% vs 31.6\% for the same-size baseline
($-$23~pp). A methodological audit of the \texttt{locale\_judge}
rejections reveals an under-reported failure mode:
capitalization-based entity extractors produce $\sim$85\% false
positives on common English sentence-initial words and
locally-canonical landmarks, which a static allowlist remediates
(global pass rate 70.1\% $\rightarrow$ 88.4\%).
\end{abstract}
